transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Time: 15:00 - 16:00 UTC (60m)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood CSM), Jenna Morris (Polaris Head of MLOps), Kevin Liu (Polaris CTO), Aisha Grant (Platform), Mark Reyes (DevOps), Priya Sen (Data Scientist)

Summary:
Quarterly business review focusing on usage trends, cost drift, reliability incidents over last quarter, and alignment on the roadmap and Dedicated pilot. Customer wants clarity on committed pricing, VPC options, and SLA for peak holiday traffic. Agreed to run a short benchmarking pilot and share SOC2 & architecture docs.

Topics Covered:
- Usage & cost trends (by product: chat, generation, embeddings)
- Reliability incidents and mitigation (late September outage + fallbacks)
- Dedicated vs Hosted for holiday season spikes
- Roadmap & upcoming features (Optimize recommendations, per-route dashboards)
- Security/compliance ask: KMS integration, audit logs, data residency
- Action items and next steps

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
00:00 Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, Diego, Lina, you good?
00:05 Diego Ramos: Yep, ready.
00:07 Jenna Morris: Hi, thanks, Jenna here for Polaris.
00:10 Kevin Liu: Kevin in, afternoon.
00:12 Samira Patel: Great, so the plan for the next hour is to run through usage/cost, reliability notes, then talk about Dedicated pilot and next steps. If we need extra time we can schedule follow-ups.
02:30 Diego Ramos: I'll start with the metrics we pulled. Overall token volume is up 35% q/q, embeddings up 50% because of the new search feature, but cost per token has drifted about 12% due to longer contexts and higher beam usage on the recommendation path.
03:05 Aisha Grant: Yeah the recommendation prompts got longer, we've been passing more context. I think that accounts for a lot.
03:30 Diego Ramos: Right, and we see the prefix cache hit rate is around 18% for the top routes. There's room to tune caching and batching which could cut your token spend by ~20%. Those are Redwood Optimize suggestions.
04:10 Priya Sen: Is that the same as the auto-batching feature? We turned on something last month but not sure if it's full kv cache.
04:30 Diego Ramos: It's related; auto-batching helps throughput but KV/prefix caching is separate and can avoid re-sending repeated context. We'll send a config suggestion.
06:00 Jenna Morris: On reliability, we had that 45-min degradation on Sept 22 where responses timed out for about three endpoints. Can you walk through root cause?
06:20 Diego Ramos: Yeah, apologies. Root cause was an autoscaler misconfig combined with a large 2x traffic spike from a partner test. Our fallback policy attempted model variant fallback but there were some routing timeouts. We pushed a fix and then incrementally increased buffer capacity.
07:00 Kevin Liu: We saw retries piling up; some of our clients surfaced 503s. We need an SLA for the holiday season and better on-call routing.
07:25 Samira Patel: Understood. For Dedicated we can offer reserved pools with a buffer and an SLA. Diego, can you outline what a Dedicated pool for Polaris would look like?
07:40 Diego Ramos: Sure. For your peak qps estimates (you shared 450 qps peak), recommended starting point is a 4-GPU Dedicated cluster with burst buckets and a 99.9% latency SLO target for 95th percentile. The tradeoff is cost — Dedicated reduces per-token compute cost by ~30% for heavy loads but adds a monthly reserved capacity fee.
08:15 Mark Reyes: Wait, we need exact numbers. What's the monthly reserve and the per-token delta?
08:25 Samira Patel: We'll send a detailed pricing spreadsheet but high level: commit tiers start at $25k/month for the starter cluster, with unit cost reductions depending on commit size. Diego will prepare an option matrix.
09:10 Priya Sen: Also on security - where is customer data stored for hosted? We need KMS integration and longer audit log retention.
09:25 Lina Cho: We support KMS/HSM and can enable longer audit retention in the Console. I'll attach the SOC2 docs and architecture diagram after the call.
09:45 Jenna Morris: Are there VPC/private deployment options? Our compliance team prefers a private control plane for PII workloads.
10:00 Diego Ramos: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options. There are pros/cons: private gives full network isolation but lengthens onboarding and you lose some multi-region seamless routing unless we set cross-region peering. We can scope that in the pilot.
11:30 Kevin Liu: For the Dedicated pilot, can we test with a small subset of traffic first and have automatic fallback to hosted? We can't risk total outage.
11:45 Diego Ramos: That's the recommended pattern — canary traffic to Dedicated with automatic fallback routing to hosted instances if latency degrades. We'll propose a rollout plan.
14:00 Priya Sen: About observability, we need per-route token-level cost breakdowns and a way to link to our internal tracing. Is the Console able to integrate with our tracing pipeline?
14:20 Samira Patel: Yes, we have tracing hooks and you can push spans into your tracing system. We'll share docs. Also the Console now shows token cost per route and per model. Some of the naming in the console might be a bit off (we shipped a label rename recently, sorry if it's confusing).
16:30 Jenna Morris: Looking at the numbers, if we do the KV cache tuning and move 20% of calls to a caching layer, what's the projected impact?
16:45 Diego Ramos: Ballpark is 18-25% reduction in tokens, which translates to ~15% total cost reduction after accounting for increased embeddings usage. We'll run a simulation and share it.
19:00 Kevin Liu: One other question — how does Redwood handle model upgrades? We are worried about regressions if you swap model variants.
19:20 Lina Cho: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval set. We can also pin model versions per route. Priya, you'll be able to upload prompt sets and evals to trigger quality monitors.
21:10 Priya Sen: Great, we'll upload top 10 prompts. We'll need per-prompt drift alerts.
21:30 Samira Patel: Noted.
23:00 Jenna Morris: On contractual terms, if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract, what's the minimum and can we do quarterly true-ups?
23:20 Samira Patel: Yes, there are 12-month commit discounts with quarterly usage reconciliation. We'll include run-rate vs committed spend examples in the pricing sheet.
25:10 Mark Reyes: For the benchmark run, can Diego's team help collect real traffic subset and run a 1-week comparison across hosted vs Dedicated? We need latency p95 and cost per 100k tokens.
25:30 Diego Ramos: Absolutely — we'll coordinate. We'll need a traffic dump (anonymized). Jenna, can you share that?
26:00 Jenna Morris: Yes, we'll share a sanitized sample by close of business Tuesday.
26:35 Samira Patel: Ok recap, action items and owners as we discussed. We'll send the SOC2 docs, pricing, Dedicated sizing options, and the config suggestions for caching.
28:00 Kevin Liu: One last quick thing — competitors. We are also talking to Bedrock and Anthropic for redundancy. How do you compare on routing and cost predictability?
28:20 Samira Patel: We focus on production predictability: clear per-route cost, rollback controls, and unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private. We'll share a short competitive note.
30:00 Jenna Morris: Thanks, appreciate it.
31:00 Samira Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items.

End of call.

References & Links Mentioned:

- Dedicated sizing options doc (Diego will draft)
